approach: Add run/format.rs with `format_work_tree(dir, changes: &[DiffEntry], ctx: &CheckContext)`. It is Athena host code, not an agent command. When `dir/Cargo.toml` is a file and the change list holds a non-deleted `*.rs` entry, it runs `cargo fmt --all` and then `cargo fmt --all --check`, both through `checks::run_check`. It returns `Skipped(reason)`, `Done` or `Unfixed{output, note}`. Per round-1 finding 1 (option a), `producer_loop` calls it in every pass, right after the producer's report has been parsed and before the first `snapshot.change_list()` (producer.rs:339). So the unmet, unchanged-file, scope, decision-gate and mirror-drift checks, `loop_replay` (producer.rs:370) and the later candidate, checks and verifier all see the same formatted tree. A pinned study (`ctx.pin_dir`) is skipped. The env comes from `athena_agent::env::build` with `Side::Produce`, matching the tree being formatted; the checks use `Side::Verify` on the verify directory. Unfixed changes no flow: a UI line is printed, and the configured `fmt` check fails on the same tree with the same rustfmt text. Root cause: the producer's grant allows `cargo fmt` (policy.rs:680 denies it only to roles that cannot write), but only prose asks the producer to run it and nothing makes the tree formatted before the gate. Tests drive real `cargo fmt` on temp crates, plus one end-to-end fake-driver job whose check is `cargo fmt --all --check`.

decisions.choice: Run the format step in each producer pass, immediately after the report is parsed (after the `raw` match, producer.rs:325-335) and before `let changes = snapshot.change_list()?` (producer.rs:339). Compute a first change list for the guard, format, and let the existing line 339 read the list again.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 1 with option (a). `loop_replay` (producer.rs:370, mod.rs:2250) stores `LoopReplay.tree`, and `replay_run` reuses it only if `covers(&tree, &ids)` holds (mod.rs:182-184, 2208-2214). Formatting after the loop would change the candidate tree, so verification would rebuild the replay pair. It would also leave the scope, gate and mirror send-back checks judging a tree that is not the candidate. With the step before line 339, every in-loop reader sees the tree that becomes the candidate, and a path the formatter adds is seen while the producer can still be sent back. It is still after the producer and before the checks and verifier, so criterion 3 holds. The step is idempotent, so a send-back pass formats again at little cost.

rejected.option: Format once after the loop, before `Ok(Flow::Go(..))`
rejected.why: The loop-replay tree no longer matches the candidate, so the replay pair is built twice. The in-loop scope, gate and mirror checks judge an unformatted tree. A formatter-added path ends the job at check_and_verify (mod.rs:1843-1862) with no send-back.
Same stale-tree problem as the post-loop placement, and it splits the producer stage across two files.

rejected.option: Format after the TimedOut or non-Success returns too
rejected.why: Those paths stop the job (producer.rs:304-316) and keep or discard the work as it is. Formatting a cut-off tree gains nothing. A tree-seeded retry is formatted when its own producer finishes.

decisions.choice: Run `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo fmt --all --check` through `crate::checks::run_check` with `CheckSpec{name:"format", kind: CheckKind::Command, skip_when_only: None}`. The env is `athena_agent::env::build(&EnvSpec{.. side: Side::Produce ..})` and the timeout is `budget.check_timeout_s`. This is the same function the checks use, called for the produce side to match the formatted tree (mod.rs:1937-1948 uses Side::Verify on the verify directory).
decisions.reason: It reuses tested code (checks.rs:513) for timeout, process-group kill, kill switch, registry, redaction and the output tail. The Unfixed output then has the shape of a failed fmt check record, which criterion 2 compares.

rejected.why: `run_bounded` drops output, so the error text of criterion 2 would be lost, and it has no kill switch or redaction.

rejected.option: Use the producer spec.env with CargoShim
rejected.why: The shim takes a build slot for build, test, clippy and check. fmt builds nothing, so a slot wait would hold the job for no reason.

decisions.choice: The step takes `&[athena_git::DiffEntry]` (fields `status: char`, `path: String`, crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs:129-137), the type `snapshot.change_list()` returns. It skips unless `dir/Cargo.toml` is a file and some entry has `status != 'D'` and a path ending in `.rs`. Every test builds `DiffEntry` values with a helper `entry(status, path)` that leaves modes and oids empty, including a `'D'` entry for the deleted-file case.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: one signature, the status is available for the deleted case, and production passes the real list unchanged. The `.rs` guard keeps a docs-only or Cargo.toml-only job from rewriting base files outside its scope.

rejected.why: Needs conversion in production, or loses the status that the deleted-file test needs.
A job with no Rust change could grow its diff by base layout drift and fail the scope check.

decisions.choice: An Unfixed result changes no flow: one UI line `format     cargo fmt --check still fails: <first line>; the fmt check will report it`, and the tree is left as it is. A UI line `format     cargo fmt rewrote the work tree before the checks` is printed when `work_tree_tree()` differs after the step.
decisions.reason: The reading says unfixable errors stay and the normal fmt check reports them. A second reporting path could relax the gate, which is out of scope.

rejected.option: Send the producer back with the rustfmt error
rejected.why: Adds a send-back class beyond one focused step. Left as a User: question.

rejected.option: Fail the job at the step
rejected.why: It would duplicate the fmt check and bypass the baseline pre-existing comparison (`mark_pre_existing`).

decisions.choice: Leave crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs and all config untouched. State the root cause correctly (finding 2): the deny at policy.rs:680 is `sub == "fmt" && !policy.writes && no --check`, so it binds only roles that cannot write, such as the verifier. The producer may already run `cargo fmt`; the fault is that only prose asked it to and nothing made the tree formatted before the gate. The step is host code spawning a process, not a Bash command through the hook.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 and Out of scope. The hook's grants are unchanged, and moving the guarantee from prose to a code step is the point of the change.

rejected.option: Change the policy to allow fmt for more roles
rejected.why: Out of scope, and the producer already has the grant.

rejected.option: Add a prompt rule telling the producer to run cargo fmt
rejected.why: Prose is the failing mechanism; the user default says enforce by mechanism.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/run/format.rs. Define `pub(super) enum Formatted { Skipped(&'static str), Done, Unfixed { output: String, note: Option<String> } }` and `pub(super) fn format_work_tree(dir: &Path, changes: &[athena_git::DiffEntry], ctx: &CheckContext<'_>) -> Result<Formatted>`. Return Skipped when `dir/Cargo.toml` is not a file or when no entry has `status != 'D'` and a path ending in `.rs`. Otherwise `run_check` a `CheckSpec{name:"format", run:["cargo","fmt","--all"], kind: CheckKind::Command, skip_when_only: None}` and ignore its pass or fail. Then `run_check` the `--check` form. Return Done if it passed, else Unfixed with the check's `output_tail` and `note`. Module docs give the root cause: the producer's grant allows `cargo fmt` (the policy.rs:680 deny binds only roles that cannot write), but only prose asks for it and nothing formats the tree before the gate.
In crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs add `mod format;` among the module declarations (lines 61-68).

In producer.rs, inside the loop after the `raw` match (line 335) and before `let unmet` (336), add the step. Skip when `ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`. Otherwise build `env` with `athena_agent::env::build(&EnvSpec{agents:&jc.config.agents, job:id.as_str(), job_dir:&job_dir, snapshot:snapshot.dir(), side:Side::Produce, capability_env:&capability_env}, |k| std::env::var(k).ok()).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?` and a `CheckContext{dir: snapshot.dir(), env:&env, timeout: Duration::from_secs(jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s), registry:&self.state.registry(), job:id.as_str(), redactor: ctx.redactor}`. Take `before = snapshot.work_tree_tree()?` and `pre = snapshot.change_list()?`, then call `format::format_work_tree(snapshot.dir(), &pre, &fctx)?`. Print `format     cargo fmt rewrote the work tree before the checks` when `work_tree_tree()` differs afterwards, and the Unfixed line (first output line) for Unfixed. Leave the existing `let changes = snapshot.change_list()?` at line 339 to read the list again. Extend the `producer_loop` doc comment.

Write the CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## [Unreleased]`: a job whose only defect is rustfmt layout reaches the verifier formatted; the root cause is that the producer may run `cargo fmt` but nothing made the tree formatted before the gate; Athena now runs `cargo fmt` then `cargo fmt --check` on the work tree after each producer pass; an unfixable error still fails the fmt check; agent policy is unchanged.

In run/tests.rs add to `produce_and_verify_order_tests`: a `FMT_CHECK` const (`["cargo","fmt","--all","--check"]` as the test check), an `entry(status: char, path: &str) -> DiffEntry` helper, a temp-crate and `CheckContext` helper, the unit tests for criteria 1, 2 and 5, and the end-to-end test for criteria 3 and 4 (`commit_file` Cargo.toml and a clean src/lib.rs, a script wrapper setting the producer turn's edits for README.md and a mis-formatted src/lib.rs, `athena_with(.., FMT_CHECK, ..)`, `go`, then assert Landed, the candidate changes, `show_file` equality and a `format` UI line).

Also run `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-agent` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle --test retry --test drain --test mirrors`. No refusal or matching rule is added or changed, so no refusal_corpus case is mapped. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is run only as a regression guard; this plan cites no corpus case ids because it read none.

risks.risk: The base is not fmt-clean, so `cargo fmt --all` rewrites files the producer never touched and adds paths outside the job's allowed paths.
risks.mitigation: The step runs only when a non-deleted `.rs` entry is already in the change list. It now runs before the in-loop scope check, so an added path is named and the producer can be sent back. The reading accepts the clean-base assumption, and the changelog bullet notes it.

risks.risk: Formatting every pass costs two cargo runs per producer invocation.
risks.mitigation: The cost is a few seconds with no build, the step is idempotent, and a producer rarely has more than two passes (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`).

risks.risk: `cargo fmt` needs cargo, rustfmt and rustup resolution under a cleared environment.
risks.mitigation: The env comes from `env::build` with the same pass lists the checks use, and the tests pass PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME. If the tool cannot start, `run_check` records a failed run with a note; the step returns Unfixed and the fmt check fails as it does today.

risks.risk: The unit tests run real cargo and need rustfmt installed.
risks.mitigation: CI already runs `cargo fmt --check`, and the temp crates have no dependencies. A missing rustfmt makes the tests fail, not skip.

risks.risk: A pinned study mounts a checkout inside the work tree (producer.rs:147-149), and formatting would alter pinned files.
rustfmt output varies by toolchain version, so literal expected text could drift.
risks.mitigation: Test 1 uses stable constructs (a long array and `fn f( )->u32{1}`) and proves success with the post `--check` pass, plus a literal only for the simple function body.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes` in run/tests.rs. It writes a temp crate (Cargo.toml and src/lib.rs with a long `pub const` array on one line and `fn f( )->u32{1}`). It builds a `CheckContext` with env PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME from the process, `Registry::new(tempdir)` and `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`. It runs `run_check` with `cargo fmt --all --check` and asserts it fails. It then calls `format_work_tree(dir, &[entry('M', "src/lib.rs")], &ctx)` and asserts the outcome is `Done`, the file text changed to the rustfmt layout, and `cargo fmt --all --check` through `run_check` now passes.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: The file bytes change to the formatted layout, the outcome is Done, and the fmt check goes from failed to passed. The whole athena-core suite passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the formatter run, the file stays mis-formatted, so the content assertion, the Done assertion and the post-`--check` assertion all fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `run::format::format_work_tree` (added by plan step 1), called with a real `CheckContext` over a tempdir and the real `cargo fmt`. Guards: Cargo.toml present and a non-deleted `.rs` entry. No double is used. `run_check` (checks.rs:513) exists. The test is added by plan step 5.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `an_unfixable_fmt_error_is_reported_and_the_fmt_check_fails_with_the_same_text`. The temp crate's src/lib.rs is `pub fn broken( {` (a parse error). It calls `format_work_tree` with an `entry('M', "src/lib.rs")` and asserts `Unfixed{output, ..}` where `output` holds a line starting `error` and the name `lib.rs`. It then runs `run_check` with the configured fmt spec (`cargo fmt --all --check`) on the same dir. It asserts `!passed` and that `output_tail` contains the step's first `error` line. It asserts the broken file is byte-identical afterwards.
demonstrations.observes: A failed fmt result whose rustfmt error text appears in the failed check's output tail. The tree is not changed and the gate is not relaxed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step swallowed the failure and returned Done, the Unfixed assertion fails. If it rewrote or deleted the broken file, the byte-identity assertion fails. If the check's output tail did not carry the error, the contains assertion fails.
